source_note: Source-grounded practice MCQs generated from text-bearing PDFs, DOCX and PPTX course files bundled in the repository. Image-only PDFs were skipped and no OCR was performed. Existing real questions were reused where available. Question-level topic tags are metadata; the current quiz UI does not filter by them yet.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about matter is correct?
options: All matter is composed of atoms
Matter can be created or destroyed
Matter has no definite shape or volume
questions.explanation: Matter is indeed composed of atoms and molecules

questions.text: Which state of matter has definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.explanation: Liquids have definite volume but take the shape of their container

questions.text: At STP, 1 mol of any gas occupies what volume?
questions.explanation: Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP is 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹

questions.text: The kinetic molecular theory states that gas particles
options: have no volume and no intermolecular forces
have significant volume and strong forces
questions.explanation: Gas particles are assumed to have negligible volume and no intermolecular forces

questions.text: Which of the following describes an endothermic process?
questions.explanation: Endothermic processes absorb heat from the surroundings

questions.text: In the reaction 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, how many moles of water are produced from 3 moles of H2?
questions.explanation: 2 mol H2 produces 2 mol H2O (ratio 1:1), so 3 mol H2 produces 3 mol H2O

questions.text: What mass of CO2 is produced when 16 g of CH4 burns completely in excess O2? (CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O)
questions.explanation: 16 g CH4 = 1 mol → 1 mol CO2 = 44 g

questions.text: What mass of O2 is needed to completely burn 16 g of CH4? (CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O)
questions.explanation: 16 g CH4 = 1 mol, needs 2 mol O2 = 64 g

questions.text: How many molecules are in 2 moles of any substance?
questions.explanation: 2 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules

questions.text: What is the molar mass of H2O? (H=1, O=16)
How many moles are in 6.02 × 10²³ molecules of H2O?
questions.explanation: 6.02 × 10²³ is Avogadro's number, so 1 mol

questions.text: What is the mass of 0.25 mol of NaCl? (Na=23, Cl=35.5)
Which of the following is a correctly balanced chemical equation?
questions.explanation: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O has equal H and O on both sides

questions.text: What is the total number of moles of products when 1 mol C3H8 reacts with excess O2? (C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O)
questions.explanation: 3 mol CO2 + 4 mol H2O = 7 mol total products

questions.text: What mass of HCl is needed to react with 10 g of NaOH? (NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O)
What is the volume of 2 mol of an ideal gas at STP? (molar volume = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹)
What volume does 0.5 mol of ideal gas occupy at STP?
According to Boyle's law, at constant temperature, the pressure of a gas is
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P ∝ 1/V at constant T

questions.text: The enthalpy change when a reaction occurs in the molar quantities shown in the chemical equation under standard conditions is called the
questions.explanation: This is the definition of standard enthalpy change of reaction

questions.text: For the reaction H2 + 1/2O2 → H2O(l), ΔHf° = -286 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the enthalpy change when 2 mol of H2O is formed?
questions.explanation: 2 mol × -286 kJ mol⁻¹ = -572 kJ

questions.text: Hess's law states that the enthalpy change for a reaction is
questions.explanation: Hess's law: ΔH is a state function, independent of pathway

questions.text: The rate law for a reaction expresses the rate as a function of
questions.explanation: Rate law: rate = k[A]m[B]n...

questions.text: For a first-order reaction, the half-life is
options: depends on the rate constant only
questions.explanation: For first-order: t½ = ln2/k, independent of [A]0

questions.text: The Arrhenius equation relates the rate constant k to
questions.explanation: k = A exp(-Ea/RT), relating k to Ea and T

questions.text: A catalyst increases the reaction rate by
questions.explanation: Catalysts speed up reactions by lowering Ea

questions.text: At equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the
questions.explanation: Dynamic equilibrium: rates are equal forward and backward

questions.text: For the reaction N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, if the volume of the container is decreased, the equilibrium will shift to the
questions.explanation: Decreasing volume increases pressure; side with fewer moles (2 vs 4) is favored, i.e., right/NH3

questions.text: The equilibrium constant Kc has which property regarding temperature?
questions.explanation: Kc depends on temperature; for exothermic reactions, Kc decreases with increasing T

questions.text: Molarity (M) is defined as the number of moles of solute per
questions.explanation: M = moles of solute / litres of solution

questions.text: What is the mole fraction of a component in a solution?
options: ratio of moles of that component to total moles of all constituents
mass of component / mass of solution
volume of component / volume of solution
moles of component / moles of solvent
questions.explanation: Xm = moles of M / (moles of M + moles of N)

questions.text: A 0.5 M solution contains how many moles of solute in 200 mL?
questions.explanation: 0.5 mol/L × 0.2 L = 0.1 mol

questions.text: pH is defined as the negative logarithm of the hydronium ion concentration: pH = -log[H3O+]. What is the pH of 0.01 M HCl? (HCl is a strong acid, fully dissociated)
What is the pOH of a solution with pH = 4?
questions.explanation: pH + pOH = 14, so pOH = 14 - 4 = 10

questions.text: What is the hydrogen ion concentration of a solution with pH = 3?
The relative atomic mass of chlorine is approximately
questions.explanation: Chlorine has isotopes 35Cl and 37Cl, average Ar ≈ 35.5 u

questions.text: In mass spectrometry, the peak representing the most abundant isotope is called the
questions.explanation: The base peak is the most intense peak in a mass spectrum, representing the most abundant fragment/ion

questions.text: The electrons in an atom occupy orbitals of fixed energy and spatial distribution, and each orbital only contains a maximum of two electrons with
questions.explanation: Pauli exclusion principle: maximum 2 electrons per orbital with opposite spins

questions.text: Which of the following statements about atomic structure is correct?
options: Electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed circular paths
Electrons occupy orbitals of fixed energy and spatial distribution
Protons and electrons have the same mass
questions.explanation: Electrons occupy orbitals (not fixed paths); Pauli exclusion principle applies

questions.text: Electrolysis is the process in which
options: electric current is used to decompose a compound into its elements
heat is used to decompose a compound
light is used to decompose a compound
catalyst is used to decompose a compound
questions.explanation: Electrolysis: electric current used to decompose compounds (e.g., molten NaCl → Na + Cl2)

questions.text: In the Bronsted-Lowry theory, an acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton
questions.explanation: Bronsted-Lowry: acid = proton donor, base = proton acceptor

questions.text: When an acid reacts with a base, the reaction is called
questions.explanation: Acid + base → salt + water, called a neutralization reaction

questions.text: The oxidation state of hydrogen in most compounds is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen usually has an oxidation state of +1 in compounds

questions.text: The oxidation state of oxygen in most compounds is
questions.explanation: Oxygen usually has an oxidation state of -2 in compounds

questions.text: Which element is oxidized in the reaction: Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu?
questions.explanation: Zn goes from oxidation state 0 to +2, losing electrons (oxidation)

questions.text: Which element is reduced in the reaction: Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu?
questions.explanation: Cu goes from +2 oxidation state to 0, gaining electrons (reduction)

questions.text: The sum of oxidation states in a neutral compound is
options: equal to the number of atoms
questions.explanation: For a neutral compound, the sum of oxidation states equals zero

questions.text: For the reaction 2NO + O2 → 2NO2, if doubling [NO] quadruples the rate and doubling [O2] doubles the rate, the rate law is
questions.explanation: Rate ∝ [NO]²[O2]¹ from the effects described

questions.text: The overall order of a reaction is the sum of the exponents in the rate law. If rate = k[A]2[B]1, the overall order is
questions.explanation: 2 + 1 = 3, so the reaction is third-order overall

questions.text: What are the units of the rate constant k for a third-order reaction? (one reactant)
questions.explanation: For nth order: units of k = (mol^(1-n) L^(n-1) s^-1), so for 3rd order: M-2 s-1

questions.text: For a second-order reaction with rate = k[A]2, the integrated rate law is
questions.explanation: For second-order: 1/[A]t = kt + 1/[A]0

questions.text: In the reaction N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, ΔH = -92 kJ. If the temperature is increased, the equilibrium shifts to the
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature favors the endothermic direction; for exothermic forward reaction, reverse is endothermic

questions.text: Adding an inert gas at constant volume to a system at equilibrium
options: always causes the reaction to stop
questions.explanation: Adding inert gas at constant volume increases total pressure but partial moles unchanged, so no shift

questions.text: If the concentration of a reactant is increased at equilibrium, the system shifts to
options: reduce the concentration of that reactant (favor products)
increase the concentration of that reactant further
depends on the order of reaction
questions.explanation: Le Chatelier: increasing reactant concentration shifts equilibrium to consume it, favoring products

questions.text: A buffer solution resists changes in pH upon addition of small amounts of
questions.explanation: Buffers contain a weak acid and its conjugate base (or weak base and conjugate acid)

questions.text: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation is pH = pKa + log([base]/[acid]). For a buffer with [base] = [acid], pH is
questions.explanation: If [base] = [acid], log(1) = 0, so pH = pKa

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "OVERALL ORDER OF REACTION: This is the sum of powers of the ______ of individual reactants."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: OVERALL ORDER OF REACTION: This is the sum of powers of the concentration of individual reactants. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What is the effect of decreasing the temperature on an ______ reaction at equilibrium?"
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: What is the effect of decreasing the temperature on an exothermic reaction at equilibrium? The missing term is 'exothermic'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The EMF is affected by changes in ______ of the reactants by energy losses due to heating of the cell and external circuit."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: The EMF is affected by changes in concentration of the reactants by energy losses due to heating of the cell and external circuit. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What is the standard ______ change of reaction for the following equation: 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(l), given the following enthalpies of formation: H2(g) = 0 kJ/mol, O2(g) = 0 kJ/mol, H2O(l) = -285.8 kJ/mol?"
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: What is the standard enthalpy change of reaction for the following equation: 2H2(g) + O2(g) → 2H2O(l), given the following enthalpies of formation: H2(g) = 0 kJ/mol, O2(g) = 0 kJ/mol, H2O(l) = -285.8 kJ/mol? The missing term is 'enthalpy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Bromothymol bluethis a weak organic acid ______ which is yellow at pH 6 and below; and blue at pH 8 and above."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Bromothymol bluethis a weak organic acid indicator which is yellow at pH 6 and below; and blue at pH 8 and above. The missing term is 'indicator'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•______, Ea,is the minimum energy required to initiate a chemical reaction."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •Activation energy, Ea,is the minimum energy required to initiate a chemical reaction. The missing term is 'activation energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The electrodes are surfaces in which ______ reduction half reaction occur."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: The electrodes are surfaces in which oxidation reduction half reaction occur. The missing term is 'oxidation'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•Law of Mass Action: The rate of a simple (one step) reaction is directly proportional to the ______ of the reacting substances."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •Law of Mass Action: The rate of a simple (one step) reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the reacting substances. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "______ Community College First-Order Processes If a reaction is first-order: a plot of ln [A]tversus twill yield a straight line with a slope of -k."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: Charles Community College First-Order Processes If a reaction is first-order: a plot of ln [A]tversus twill yield a straight line with a slope of -k. The missing term is 'Charles'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What mass of copper will be deposited at the cathode from the ______ of aqueous copper sulfate using a current of 0.50 A for 30 minutes?"
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: What mass of copper will be deposited at the cathode from the electrolysis of aqueous copper sulfate using a current of 0.50 A for 30 minutes? The missing term is 'electrolysis'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Voltaic cell is always denoted as Zn(s)/ Zn2+(aq)//Cu2+(aq)/Cu(s) The components of the anode(______ half cell) is on the left and that of the cathode is on the right."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Voltaic cell is always denoted as Zn(s)/ Zn2+(aq)//Cu2+(aq)/Cu(s) The components of the anode(oxidation half cell) is on the left and that of the cathode is on the right. The missing term is 'oxidation'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What are the electrodes made of in the ______ of molten sodium chloride?"
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: What are the electrodes made of in the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride? The missing term is 'electrolysis'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Plan We recall that one ______ of CH4 reacts with two moles of O2."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Plan We recall that one mole of CH4 reacts with two moles of O2. The missing term is 'mole'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "- A) ______ - B) Electroplating - C) Electromagnetism - D) Electrostatics 4."
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: - A) Electrolysis - B) Electroplating - C) Electromagnetism - D) Electrostatics 4. The missing term is 'electrolysis'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Instead, gaseous H2 and aqueous OHions are produced by ______ of H2O molecules at the cathode."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Instead, gaseous H2 and aqueous OHions are produced by reduction of H2O molecules at the cathode. The missing term is 'reduction'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What is the order of a reaction that has a half-life that is independent of the initial ______ of reactants?"
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: What is the order of a reaction that has a half-life that is independent of the initial concentration of reactants? The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The REDOX reactions which involve loss of electrons(oxidation) and gain of electrons(reduction) are the major reactions in ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: The REDOX reactions which involve loss of electrons(oxidation) and gain of electrons(reduction) are the major reactions in electrolysis. The missing term is 'electrolysis'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "+ constant For exothermic reactions, K decreases with an increase in temperature but for ______, K increases with an increase in temperature."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: + constant For exothermic reactions, K decreases with an increase in temperature but for endothermic, K increases with an increase in temperature. The missing term is 'endothermic'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Then we use the actual (isolated) yield and the previous definition to calculate the ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Then we use the actual (isolated) yield and the previous definition to calculate the percent yield. The missing term is 'percent yield'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "- A) A reaction that absorbs heat from the surroundings and has a positive ______ change."
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: - A) A reaction that absorbs heat from the surroundings and has a positive enthalpy change. The missing term is 'enthalpy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "1/[A]t Time (s) (slope= k) Dan Reid Champaign CHS Second-Order Processes Half Life Half-Life •Half-lifeis the time taken for the ______ of a reactant to drop to half its original value."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: 1/[A]t Time (s) (slope= k) Dan Reid Champaign CHS Second-Order Processes Half Life Half-Life •Half-lifeis the time taken for the concentration of a reactant to drop to half its original value. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•Notice that if a forward reaction is exothermic… (CH3NC àCH3CN), then the reverse reaction is ______… (CH3CN àCH3NC)."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •Notice that if a forward reaction is exothermic… (CH3NC àCH3CN), then the reverse reaction is endothermic… (CH3CN àCH3NC). The missing term is 'endothermic'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "In general, the greater the rate constant K, the faster the ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: In general, the greater the rate constant K, the faster the reaction rate. The missing term is 'reaction rate'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "______ of molten sodium chloride (DOWNS CELL) Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Electrolysis of molten sodium chloride (DOWNS CELL) Solid sodium chloride does not conduct electricity. The missing term is 'electrolysis'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "- C) A reaction that releases heat to the surroundings and has a positive ______ change."
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: - C) A reaction that releases heat to the surroundings and has a positive enthalpy change. The missing term is 'enthalpy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Cu2+ + 2e- →Cu(s)---------------reduction Zn(s)→Zn2+ + 2e- -----------______ Cu2+ + Zn → Cu + Zn2+ This is the basis of voltaic cell."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Cu2+ + 2e- →Cu(s)---------------reduction Zn(s)→Zn2+ + 2e- -----------oxidation Cu2+ + Zn → Cu + Zn2+ This is the basis of voltaic cell. The missing term is 'oxidation'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•In the preceding peroxide decomposition example, in the absence of a ______, H2O2decomposes directly to water and oxygen."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •In the preceding peroxide decomposition example, in the absence of a catalyst, H2O2decomposes directly to water and oxygen. The missing term is 'catalyst'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "-3rdorder…doubling ______ leads to 23 (or 8 times) the rate."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: -3rdorder…doubling concentration leads to 23 (or 8 times) the rate. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The ______ (Kc) has a constant value at a given temperature independent of original concentration ,volume of container or pressure The Kc depends on the way the equation is written."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: The equilibrium constant (Kc) has a constant value at a given temperature independent of original concentration ,volume of container or pressure The Kc depends on the way the equation is written. The missing term is 'equilibrium constant'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "- D) It depends on the ______ and pressure of the system."
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: - D) It depends on the concentration and pressure of the system. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "______ Community College Reaction Mechanisms Reaction Mechanisms The sequence of events that describes the actual process by which reactants become products is called the reaction mechanism."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: Charles Community College Reaction Mechanisms Reaction Mechanisms The sequence of events that describes the actual process by which reactants become products is called the reaction mechanism. The missing term is 'Charles'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•From ______, we know that as temperature increases, the total kinetic energy increases and the number of molecules with energy greater than Eaincreases."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •From kinetic molecular theory, we know that as temperature increases, the total kinetic energy increases and the number of molecules with energy greater than Eaincreases. The missing term is 'kinetic molecular theory'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Generally, band gaps vary with position in the ______, but tend to decrease with increasing MW of the semiconductor."
questions.explanation: From 1585238250.pdf: Generally, band gaps vary with position in the periodic table, but tend to decrease with increasing MW of the semiconductor. The missing term is 'periodic table'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "______ Community College Catalysts A catalystis a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself being consumed."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: Charles Community College Catalysts A catalystis a substance that increases the rate of a chemical reaction without itself being consumed. The missing term is 'Charles'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "This is because a standard electrode potential always refers to a half reaction written as ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: This is because a standard electrode potential always refers to a half reaction written as reduction. The missing term is 'reduction'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What is the order of a reaction that has a ______ of the form rate = k[A]2[B]2?"
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: What is the order of a reaction that has a rate law of the form rate = k[A]2[B]2? The missing term is 'rate law'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "What is the effect of increasing the ______ of a reactant on a system at equilibrium?"
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: What is the effect of increasing the concentration of a reactant on a system at equilibrium? The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "An ______ reaction is one that absorbs heat energy from the surroundings."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: An endothermic reaction is one that absorbs heat energy from the surroundings. The missing term is 'endothermic'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "______ of NaCl in the Downs cell is the main commercial method of producing metallic sodium."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Electrolysis of NaCl in the Downs cell is the main commercial method of producing metallic sodium. The missing term is 'electrolysis'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Equilibria: ______ , Factors affecting equilibrium , Le’ Chaterlier’s principle."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Equilibria: Chemical equilibrium , Factors affecting equilibrium , Le’ Chaterlier’s principle. The missing term is 'chemical equilibrium'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "A pale green gas, which is chlorine, Cl2, is liberated at one ______."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: A pale green gas, which is chlorine, Cl2, is liberated at one electrode. The missing term is 'electrode'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Chemists use a unit called ______ for counting the number of particles (including atoms, molecules, ions and electrons) in substances."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Chemists use a unit called mole for counting the number of particles (including atoms, molecules, ions and electrons) in substances. The missing term is 'mole'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "This means that 1 ______ of electrons has a charge of 9.649 X 104 C and this is called faraday constant."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: This means that 1 mole of electrons has a charge of 9.649 X 104 C and this is called faraday constant. The missing term is 'mole'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Notation for ______: [A] = concentration of reactant A [B] = concentration of reactant B •John D."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: Notation for Stoichiometry: [A] = concentration of reactant A [B] = concentration of reactant B •John D. The missing term is 'stoichiometry'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "How does the value of the rate constant k change with temperature for an ______ reaction?"
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: How does the value of the rate constant k change with temperature for an endothermic reaction? The missing term is 'endothermic'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Faraday states that the amount of substance that undergoes oxidation or reduction at each electrode during ______ is directly proportional to the amount of electricity that passes through the cell."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Faraday states that the amount of substance that undergoes oxidation or reduction at each electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the amount of electricity that passes through the cell. The missing term is 'electrolysis'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "In ______, the total energy stored in a substance is called the HEAT CONTENT OR ENTHALPY, with symbol, H."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: In thermochemistry, the total energy stored in a substance is called the HEAT CONTENT OR ENTHALPY, with symbol, H. The missing term is 'thermochemistry'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•For reactions follow simple rate laws: v = k [A]m [B]n… -[A], [B]: reactant concentrations -The exponents mand n: ______ (w.r.t."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •For reactions follow simple rate laws: v = k [A]m [B]n… -[A], [B]: reactant concentrations -The exponents mand n: reaction order (w.r.t. The missing term is 'reaction order'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•The Eafor the reaction is lowered, thus the ______ increases."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •The Eafor the reaction is lowered, thus the reaction rate increases. The missing term is 'reaction rate'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "______ Community College First-Order Processes •When ln[A] is plotted as a function of time, a straight line results."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: Charles Community College First-Order Processes •When ln[A] is plotted as a function of time, a straight line results. The missing term is 'Charles'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "If we run n right up to ______'s number, we expect to obtain No MOs, ranging from fully bonding (+++++...) to fully antibonding (+-+-+-...), with a whole bunch of other MOs between these extremes."

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Before we study the concept of the limiting reactant in ______, let’s develop the basic idea by considering a simple but analogous nonchemical example."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Before we study the concept of the limiting reactant in stoichiometry, let’s develop the basic idea by considering a simple but analogous nonchemical example. The missing term is 'stoichiometry'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "= 20/180 = 0.11mol C6H12O6 H2O = 18 g/mol 18g water = 1 ______ 80g = ?"
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: = 20/180 = 0.11mol C6H12O6 H2O = 18 g/mol 18g water = 1 mole 80g = ? The missing term is 'mole'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "A zeroth (or zero) order reaction is the one that the rate of reaction is independent of the ______ of the reactant."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: A zeroth (or zero) order reaction is the one that the rate of reaction is independent of the concentration of the reactant. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•Just as a ball cannot get over a hill if it does not roll up the hill with enough energy, a reaction cannot occur unless the molecules possess sufficient energy to get over the ______ barrier."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •Just as a ball cannot get over a hill if it does not roll up the hill with enough energy, a reaction cannot occur unless the molecules possess sufficient energy to get over the activation energy barrier. The missing term is 'activation energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Metallic sodium is produced by ______ of Na+ ions at the cathode, where electrons are being forced into the cell."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Metallic sodium is produced by reduction of Na+ ions at the cathode, where electrons are being forced into the cell. The missing term is 'reduction'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Reaction speed: measured by the change in ______ with time."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: Reaction speed: measured by the change in concentration with time. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Ea k uncatalyzed catalyzed ratecatalyzed> rateuncatalyzed Chung (Peter) Chieh University of Waterloo Catalysts •Catalysts increase the rate of a reaction by decreasing the ______ of the reaction."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: Ea k uncatalyzed catalyzed ratecatalyzed> rateuncatalyzed Chung (Peter) Chieh University of Waterloo Catalysts •Catalysts increase the rate of a reaction by decreasing the activation energy of the reaction. The missing term is 'activation energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "- D) A reaction that releases heat to the surroundings and has a negative ______ change."
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: - D) A reaction that releases heat to the surroundings and has a negative enthalpy change. The missing term is 'enthalpy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•The ______ Eais the difference in energy between reactants, CH3NC, and the transition state."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •The activation energy Eais the difference in energy between reactants, CH3NC, and the transition state. The missing term is 'activation energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Reduction reactions occur at the cathode (electrons are gained) and ______ reactions occur at the anode."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Reduction reactions occur at the cathode (electrons are gained) and oxidation reactions occur at the anode. The missing term is 'oxidation'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The balanced equation for the reaction may be written as EXAMPLE 10 ______ A 15.6-gram sample of C6H6 is mixed with excess HNO3."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: The balanced equation for the reaction may be written as EXAMPLE 10 Percent Yield A 15.6-gram sample of C6H6 is mixed with excess HNO3. The missing term is 'percent yield'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "The figure (b) shows the Downs cell that is used for the industrial ______ of sodium chloride."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: The figure (b) shows the Downs cell that is used for the industrial electrolysis of sodium chloride. The missing term is 'electrolysis'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "•The methyl isonitrile molecule needs to gain enough energy to overcome the ______ barrier."
questions.explanation: From Share KineticsOverview.pdf: •The methyl isonitrile molecule needs to gain enough energy to overcome the activation energy barrier. The missing term is 'activation energy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Rate Slope = 0 [A] Zeroth order reaction FIRST ORDER REACTION: For a first order reaction, the rate is directly proportional to the ______ of the reactant."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Rate Slope = 0 [A] Zeroth order reaction FIRST ORDER REACTION: For a first order reaction, the rate is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactant. The missing term is 'concentration'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "This shows that the reaction involves the reduction of Cu2+ to Cu metal and ______ of Zn to Zn2+."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: This shows that the reaction involves the reduction of Cu2+ to Cu metal and oxidation of Zn to Zn2+. The missing term is 'oxidation'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "At cathode: 2H+ (aq) + 2eH2 (g) To give 1 ______ of hydrogen gas, 2 moles of electrons i.e 2F are required."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: At cathode: 2H+ (aq) + 2eH2 (g) To give 1 mole of hydrogen gas, 2 moles of electrons i.e 2F are required. The missing term is 'mole'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "- C) The ______ change when a reaction occurs in any quantities under standard conditions."
questions.explanation: From Tutorial Questions for CHM 111 (1-5).pdf: - C) The enthalpy change when a reaction occurs in any quantities under standard conditions. The missing term is 'enthalpy'.

questions.text: Which term correctly completes this statement from the course notes? "Plan The balanced equation tells us that one ______ of CH4 reacts with two moles of O2."
questions.explanation: From Share CHM 111-INTRODUCTORY PHYSICAL CHEMISTRY-1.docx: Plan The balanced equation tells us that one mole of CH4 reacts with two moles of O2. The missing term is 'mole'.
